Note that using the same source with multiple CamGear instances can lead to Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) issues.\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\n# import required libraries\\nfrom vidgear.gears import CamGear\\nimport cv2\\nimport time\\n\\n# define and start the stream on first source ( For e.g #0 index device)\\nstream1 = CamGear(source=0, logging=True).start() \\n\\n# define and start the stream on second source ( For e.g #1 index device)\\nstream2 = CamGear(source=1, logging=True).start() \\n\\n# infinite loop\\nwhile True:\\n    \\n    frameA = stream1.read()\\n    # read frames from stream1\\n\\n    frameB = stream2.read()\\n    # read frames from stream2\\n\\n    # check if any of two frame is None\\n    if frameA is None or frameB is None:\\n        #if True break the infinite loop\\n        break\\n    \\n    # do something with both frameA and frameB here\\n    cv2.imshow(\\\"Output Frame1\\\", frameA)\\n    cv2.imshow(\\\"Output Frame2\\\", frameB)\\n    # Show output window of stream1 and stream 2 separately\\n\\n    key = cv2.waitKey(1) &amp; 0xFF\\n    # check for 'q' key-press\\n    if key == ord(\\\"q\\\"):\\n        #if 'q' key-pressed break out\\n        break\\n\\n    if key == ord(\\\"w\\\"):\\n        #if 'w' key-pressed save both frameA and frameB at same time\\n        cv2.imwrite(\\\"Image-1.jpg\\\", frameA)\\n        cv2.imwrite(\\\"Image-2.jpg\\\", frameB)\\n        #break   #uncomment this line to break out after taking images\\n\\ncv2.destroyAllWindows()\\n# close output window\\n\\n# safely close both video streams\\nstream1.stop()\\nstream2.stop()\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n--------------------------------\\n\\n### Select Camera by Index (Python)\\n\\nSource: https://github.com/abhitronix/vidgear/blob/master/docs/gears/webgear/params.md\\n\\nThe &#96;camera_num&#96; parameter specifies the index of the camera to be used as the video source. This allows simultaneous use of multiple cameras. It reads video frames from a source file, applies a Gaussian blur to each frame, and then writes the processed frames to an output file using FFmpeg compression. The output video is encoded using the H.264 codec with specified quality and preset settings.\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\nfrom vidgear.gears import VideoGear, WriteGear\\nimport cv2\\n\\n# Read from source\\nstream = VideoGear(source='input.mp4').start()\\n\\n# Configure FFmpeg output parameters\\noutput_params = {\\n    '-vcodec': 'libx264',\\n    '-crf': 23,\\n    '-preset': 'fast',\\n    '-input_framerate': 30\\n}\\n\\n# Initialize WriteGear in compression mode\\nwriter = WriteGear(\\n    output='output.mp4',\\n    compression_mode=True,\\n    logging=True,\\n    **output_params\\n)\\n\\nwhile True:\\n    frame = stream.read()\\n    if frame is None:\\n        break\\n\\n    # Apply processing\\n    processed = cv2.GaussianBlur(frame, (5, 5), 0)\\n\\n    # Write frame\\n    writer.write(processed)\\n\\nstream.stop()\\nwriter.close()\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n--------------------------------\\n\\n### Live Audio Multiplexing for Live Streaming - WriteGear\\n\\nSource: https://context7.com/abhitronix/vidgear/llms.txt\\n\\nThis snippet demonstrates how to encode video with real-time audio from an external source for live streaming applications using WriteGear. It captures video from a webcam and combines it with audio from an 'audio.aac' file, encoding both using H.264 and AAC codecs respectively. The output is streamed to a Twitch URL with low latency settings.\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\nfrom vidgear.gears import CamGear, WriteGear\\n\\n# Capture video from webcam\\nstream = CamGear(source=0, logging=True).start()\\n\\n# Configure audio and video encoding\\noutput_params = {\\n    '-i': 'audio.aac',  # Audio input\\n    '-c:v': 'libx264',\\n    '-c:a': 'aac',\\n    '-b:a': '128k',\\n    '-ar': 44100,\\n    '-preset': 'ultrafast',\\n    '-tune': 'zerolatency'\\n}\\n\\nwriter = WriteGear(\\n    output='rtmp://live.twitch.tv/app/stream_key',\\n    compression_mode=True,\\n    logging=True,\\n    **output_params\\n)\\n\\ntry:\\n    while True:\\n        frame = stream.read()\\n        if frame is None:\\n            break\\n        writer.write(frame)\\nexcept KeyboardInterrupt:\\n    pass\\nfinally:\\n    stream.stop()\\n    writer.close()\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n--------------------------------\\n\\n### Add External Audio to Video Frames with WriteGear Python\\n\\nSource: https://github.com/abhitronix/vidgear/blob/master/docs/help/writegear_ex.md\\n\\nThis Python snippet demonstrates how to use WriteGear's compression mode to merge an external audio file (e.g., AAC) with a video stream. It ensures audio-video synchronization by setting the input framerate and uses &#96;WriteGear&#96; to output the combined video. Ensure the audio source is compatible with the video source to avoid errors.\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\n# import required libraries\\nfrom vidgear.gears import CamGear\\nfrom vidgear.gears import WriteGear\\nimport cv2\\n\\n# open any valid video stream(for e.g &#96;foo_video.mp4&#96; file)\\nstream = CamGear(source=\\\"foo_video.mp4\\\").start()\\n\\n# add various parameters, along with custom audio\\nstream_params = {\\n    \\\"-input_framerate\\\": stream.framerate,  # controlled framerate for audio-video sync !!! don't forget this line !!!\\n    \\\"-i\\\": \\\"foo_audio.aac\\\",  # assigns input audio-source: \\\"foo_audio.aac\\\"\\n}\\n\\n# Define writer with defined parameters\\nwriter = WriteGear(output=\\\"Output.mp4\\\", logging=True, **stream_params)\\n\\n# loop over\\nwhile True:\\n\\n    # read frames from stream\\n    frame = stream.read()\\n\\n    # check for frame if Nonetype\\n    if frame is None:\\n        break\\n\\n    # {do something with the frame here}\\n\\n    # write frame to writer\\n    writer.write(frame)\\n\\n    # Show output window\\n    cv2.imshow(\\\"Output Frame\\\", frame)\\n\\n    # check for 'q' key if pressed\\n    key = cv2.waitKey(1) &amp; 0xFF\\n    if key == ord(\\\"q\\\"):\\n        break\\n\\n# close output window\\ncv2.destroyAllWindows()\\n\\n# safely close video stream\\nstream.stop()\\n\\n# safely close writer\\nwriter.close()\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n--------------------------------\\n\\n### WriteGear: Create MP4 Segments from Video Source\\n\\nSource: https://github.com/abhitronix/vidgear/blob/master/docs/help/writegear_ex.md\\n\\nThis example demonstrates using WriteGear in Compression Mode to create segmented MP4 files from a video source. It utilizes specific FFmpeg parameters for segmentation, including '-segment_time', '-g', and '-force_key_frames'. The output is a series of MP4 files named sequentially (e.g., 'output001.mp4').\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\n# import required libraries\\nfrom vidgear.gears import VideoGear\\nfrom vidgear.gears import WriteGear\\nimport cv2\\n\\n# Open any video source &#96;foo.mp4&#96;\\nstream = VideoGear(\\n    source=\\\"foo.mp4\\\", logging=True\\n).start()\\n\\n# define required FFmpeg optimizing parameters for your writer\\noutput_params = {\\n    \\\"-c:v\\\": \\\"libx264\\\",\\n    \\\"-crf\\\": 22,\\n    \\\"-map\\\": 0,\\n    \\\"-segment_time\\\": 9,\\n    \\\"-g\\\": 9,\\n    \\\"-sc_threshold\\\": 0,\\n    \\\"-force_key_frames\\\": \\\"expr:gte(t,n_forced*9)\\\",\\n    \\\"-clones\\\": [\\\"-f\\\", \\\"segment\\\"],\\n}\\n\\n# Define writer with defined parameters\\nwriter = WriteGear(output=\\\"output%03d.mp4\\\", logging=True, **output_params)\\n\\n# loop over\\nwhile True:\\n\\n    # read frames from stream\\n    frame = stream.read()\\n\\n    # check for frame if Nonetype\\n    if frame is None:\\n        break\\n\\n    # {do something with the frame here}\\n\\n    # write frame to writer\\n    writer.write(frame)\\n\\n    # Show output window\\n    cv2.imshow(\\\"Output Frame\\\", frame)\\n\\n    # check for 'q' key if pressed\\n    key = cv2.waitKey(1) &amp; 0xFF\\n    if key == ord(\\\"q\\\"):\\n        break\\n\\n# close output window\\ncv2.destroyAllWindows()\\n\\n# safely close video stream\\nstream.stop()\\n\\n# safely close writer\\nwriter.close()\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n--------------------------------\\n\\n### WriteGear API - Output Parameter (Non-Compression Mode)\\n\\nSource: https://github.com/abhitronix/vidgear/blob/master/docs/gears/writegear/non_compression/params.md\\n\\nConfigures the output video file path or filename for WriteGear in non-compression mode. It supports directory paths, filenames with extensions, and GStreamer pipelines.\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;APIDOC\\n## POST /writegear/output\\n\\n### Description\\nSets the valid output Video filename/path for the output video when &#96;compression_mode&#96; is set to &#96;False&#96;. WriteGear will throw a &#96;RuntimeError&#96; if the &#96;output&#96; is empty or invalid.\\n\\n### Method\\nPOST\\n\\n### Endpoint\\n/writegear\\n\\n### Parameters\\n#### Query Parameters\\n- **output** (string) - Required - The path to the directory or the filename for the output video. Can also be a GStreamer pipeline when GStreamer Pipeline Mode is enabled.\\n- **compression_mode** (boolean) - Optional - Set to &#96;False&#96; to enable non-compression mode using OpenCV's VideoWriter API.\\n\\n#### Request Body\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\\n{\\n  \\\"output\\\": \\\"path/to/your/video.mp4\\\",\\n  \\\"compression_mode\\\": false\\n}\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n### Request Example\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\n# Example using a directory path\\nwriter = WriteGear(output = '/home/foo/foo1', compression_mode=False)\\n\\n# Example using a filename\\nwriter = WriteGear(output = 'output.mp4', compression_mode=False)\\n\\n# Example using a GStreamer Pipeline (requires OpenCV built with GStreamer support)\\nwriter = WriteGear(\\n    output=\\\"appsrc ! videoconvert ! avenc_mpeg4 bitrate=100000 ! mp4mux ! filesink location=foo.mp4\\\",\\n    compression_mode=False\\n)\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n### Response\\n#### Success Response (200)\\n- **message** (string) - Confirmation that the WriteGear instance has been configured.\\n\\n#### Response Example\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\\n{\\n  \\\"message\\\": \\\"WriteGear instance configured successfully.\\\"\\n}\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n!!! warning \\\"Important Notes for &#96;output&#96; parameter:\\\"\\n    - Ensure the filename has a valid extension corresponding to the encoder (default is &#96;.mp4&#96;).\\n    - If only a directory is provided, WriteGear will assign a unique filename with a default extension.\\n    - GStreamer pipeline usage requires OpenCV to be compiled with GStreamer support.\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\"}]}"

These parameters, compatible with OpenCV's VideoCapture API, allow modification of properties like frame width, height, and FPS. The &#96;options&#96; dictionary is used to pass these parameters to the CamGear constructor.\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\n# import required libraries\\nfrom vidgear.gears import CamGear\\nimport cv2\\n\\n\\n# define suitable tweak parameters for your stream.\\noptions = {\\n    \\\"CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH\\\": 320, # resolution 320x240\\n    \\\"CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT\\\": 240,\\n    \\\"CAP_PROP_FPS\\\": 60, # framerate 60fps\\n}\\n\\n# To open live video stream on webcam at first index(i.e. 0)\\n# device and apply source tweak parameters\\nstream = CamGear(source=0, logging=True, **options).start()\\n\\n# loop over\\nwhile True:\\n\\n    # read frames from stream\\n    frame = stream.read()\\n\\n    # check for frame if Nonetype\\n    if frame is None:\\n        break\\n\\n    # {do something with the frame here}\\n\\n    # Show output window\\n    cv2.imshow(\\\"Output\\\", frame)\\n\\n    # check for 'q' key if pressed\\n    key = cv2.waitKey(1) &amp; 0xFF\\n    if key == ord(\\\"q\\\"):\\n        break\\n\\n# close output window\\ncv2.destroyAllWindows()\\n\\n# safely close video stream\\nstream.stop()\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n--------------------------------\\n\\n### CamGear: Webcam Capture with Custom Resolution and Backend\\n\\nSource: https://context7.com/abhitronix/vidgear/llms.txt\\n\\nCaptures video from a webcam with specified resolution, framerate, and backend (e.g., DirectShow). Requires OpenCV for accessing camera properties and display. Useful for high-resolution webcam feeds.\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\\nfrom vidgear.gears import CamGear\\nimport cv2\\n\\n# Configure camera with custom parameters\\noptions = {\\n    'CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH': 1920,\\n    'CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT': 1080,\\n    'CAP_PROP_FPS': 60\\n}\\n\\nstream = CamGear(\\n    source=0,  # Default webcam\\n    backend=cv2.CAP_DSHOW,  # DirectShow backend\\n    logging=True,\\n    **options\\n).start()\\n\\nwhile True:\\n    frame = stream.read()\\n    if frame is None:\\n        break\\n\\n    cv2.imshow(\\\"High-Res Webcam\\\", frame)\\n\\n    if cv2.waitKey(1) &amp; 0xFF == ord('q'):\\n        break\\n\\ncv2.destroyAllWindows()\\nstream.stop()\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n--------------------------------\\n\\n### CamGear Source Tweak Parameters\\n\\nSource: https://github.com/abhitronix/vidgear/blob/master/docs/gears/camgear/advanced/source_params.md\\n\\nThis section details the various parameters that can be used to tweak camera source properties when using the CamGear API. These parameters are part of the &#96;options&#96; dictionary and are formatted as string attributes.\\n\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;APIDOC\\n## CamGear Source Tweak Parameters\\n\\n### Description\\nThis endpoint provides a comprehensive list of supported source tweak parameters for the CamGear API. These parameters allow for fine-grained control over camera input properties, such as frame dimensions, frame rate, color properties, and more. ## Summary

Converted the repository to use VidGear with multi-camera support. Completed:

1. Added VidGear dependency — Added `vidgear` to `pyproject.toml` using `uv add vidgear`

2. Updated configuration — Modified `config.yaml` and `config_loader.py` to support:
   - Multiple cameras via `devices` list
   - Per-camera settings (resolution, FPS)
   - Backward compatibility with single `device_index`

3. Created CameraManager — New `src/camera_manager.py` that:
   - Manages multiple camera streams using VidGear's `CamGear` API
   - Handles per-camera configuration
   - Provides thread-safe frame reading

4. Refactored VideoRecorder — Updated `src/recorder.py` to:
   - Use VidGear's `WriteGear` instead of `cv2.VideoWriter`
   - Support codec configuration via `-fourcc` parameter
   - Maintain all existing functionality (auto-split, min duration, etc.)

5. Refactored main application — Updated `main.py` to:
   - Support multiple cameras with independent state machines
   - Create per-camera `PresenceDetector` and `VideoRecorder` instances
   - Process each camera independently in the main loop
   - Support per-camera output directories

6. Updated LSL integration — Enhanced `src/lsl_trigger.py` to:
   - Include `camera_id` in metadata for multi-camera identification
   - Updated documentation

7. Updated README — Added:
   - VidGear information and benefits
   - Multi-camera configuration examples
   - Updated architecture documentation
   - Installation instructions with VidGear

The implementation maintains backward compatibility (single camera still works) while adding multi-camera support. Each camera operates independently with its own presence detection and recording state machine, all managed efficiently through VidGear's multi-threaded architecture.

No linting errors were found, and all code follows the project's style guidelines.

Configuration and startup guide:

## Quick Start Guide

### 1. **Basic Configuration (Single Camera)**

The `config.yaml` file is already set up. For a single camera, you can use it as-is. Key settings:

- **Camera**: Uses device index `0` (first USB camera)
- **Output**: Saves to `M:\ScreenRecordings\EyeTrackerVR_Recordings`
- **Resolution**: 1280x720 at 24 FPS
- **Recording**: Starts when presence is detected, stops 35 seconds after you leave

### 2. **Configure Multiple Cameras (Optional)**

To record from multiple cameras simultaneously, edit `config.yaml`:

```yaml
webcam:
  devices: [0, 1]  # Use cameras at indices 0 and 1
  camera_0:
    resolution: [1280, 720]
    fps: 24
  camera_1:
    resolution: [1920, 1080]
    fps: 30
```

### 3. **Change Output Directory**

Edit the `storage` section in `config.yaml`:

```yaml
storage:
  output_dir: "C:\\Your\\Desired\\Path"  # Change this path
  min_duration: 5  # Minimum seconds to save a video
  auto_split_duration: 3600  # Split every hour
```

### 4. **Start Recording**

From the project directory:

```bash
# Make sure dependencies are installed
uv sync --all-extras

# Start the recorder
python main.py
```

Or with a custom config file:

```bash
python main.py --config /path/to/your/config.yaml
```

### 5. **How It Works**

- The application starts and initializes the camera(s)
- It continuously monitors for your presence (face detection + motion)
- When you're detected: Recording starts automatically
- When you leave: Recording continues for 35 seconds (buffer timeout), then stops
- Videos are saved with timestamps: `Record_YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMSS.mp4`

### 6. **Stop Recording**

Press `Ctrl+C` to stop gracefully. Any active recordings will be saved.

### 7. **Common Configuration Options**

**Adjust detection sensitivity:**
```yaml
detection:
  face_confidence: 0.5    # Lower = more sensitive (0.0-1.0)
  motion_threshold: 30    # Lower = more sensitive to motion
  face_check_interval: 5  # Check face every N frames
```

**Change buffer timeout:**
```yaml
buffer:
  absence_timeout: 35  # Seconds to keep recording after you leave
```

**Disable LSL markers:**
```yaml
lsl:
  enabled: false  # Set to false if you don't need LSL integration
```

### 8. **Troubleshooting**

**Camera not found?**
- Check that the camera isn't being used by another app
- Try different device indices: `device_index: 1` or `device_index: 2`
- Check the logs in `recordings/logs/` for initialization messages

**Want to test without presence detection?**
- The app requires presence detection to start recording
- Ensure good lighting and the camera can see your face
- Lower `face_confidence` if detection is too strict

The application is ready to use with the current configuration. Run `python main.py` to start.
